Maia for People

Fast policy answers. Human people decisions.

Maia helps employees find current guidance and helps People teams coordinate routine onboarding work. Sensitive exceptions route to the right person instead of becoming a channel answer.

All teams ↗

Give employees the current policy

People teams answer the same policy questions many times, but the correct response may depend on location, role, effective date, or a private circumstance. Maia can retrieve the approved policy, cite the relevant section, and state when the document does not cover the question.

The employee gets a direct answer for routine guidance and a clear path to a person for exceptions. Maia does not decide leave, accommodation, compensation, performance, or employee relations matters.

Coordinate onboarding in one thread

Provide the role, location, start date, current onboarding template, and owner map. Maia can prepare a checklist covering equipment, account access, required reading, introductions, and first-week milestones. Each item should show its source and responsible person.

The People partner reviews any role-specific additions, while IT and the hiring manager own their tasks. A scheduled reminder can surface missing owners or overdue preparation without exposing private employee details in a broad channel.

Prepare interview logistics

Maia can assemble approved interview guidance, the schedule, interviewer roles, and the job-specific rubric. It can draft reminders and identify a missing panel assignment or conflicting time.

The hiring team chooses candidates, evaluates evidence, and makes every employment decision. Keep candidate records and feedback within their authorized audience. Maia's role is administrative preparation, not ranking people.

Route sensitive questions safely

An employee may begin with a simple policy question that becomes personal. Configure the workflow to recognize when a public answer is inappropriate and provide a private route to the People team. The handoff can include the policy topic and the employee's own words without broadcasting the details.

Approved general guidance can stay in the channel. Individual cases move to a person with the right access and responsibility.

Keep policy versions clear

Give Maia the current policy set with effective dates and an owner. If two versions conflict, the answer should show the conflict rather than select the newer-looking file by assumption. The policy owner confirms which source is active.

Reusable channel guidance can describe where general questions belong and which topics require private handling. This helps employees know what to expect before they ask.

Start with onboarding and one policy

Use two policy versions and an onboarding case with one location-specific exception. Verify the citations, effective date, owners, and private escalation. This provides a clear measure of whether the workflow handles routine guidance without crossing into people judgment.

For onboarding, the thread can also give a new employee one clear view of what happens next without exposing internal notes. The hiring manager sees their introductions, IT sees setup tasks, and People sees the forms or policy questions that still need attention.

Questions from People teams

Does Maia make employment decisions?

No. Hiring, performance, compensation, leave, accommodation, and employee relations decisions remain with authorized people.

Can employees ask Maia privately?

Maia can work in an appropriate private context when configured. Define which topics should route directly to a People partner.

How does Maia choose a policy version?

Supply approved documents with effective dates and an owner. Maia should cite the version used and flag any conflict for review.
